clue.text: Teach heavyweight attachments and relaxed behaviors

blocks.note: to inform someone is to teach them facts
Muhammad Ali, the heavyweight boxing champion
ties are things that attach or bind

explanation.surface: Someone instructs a big, powerful person to drop formal habits and loosen up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavyweight' looks like an adjective for the teacher's subject, but it names one famous boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: Informalities are casual, unceremonious ways of acting, which is what relaxed behaviors are.

clue.text: At home with a prince, editor did not emulate Bill Clinton

blocks.note: in means at home
Prince Hal, from Shakespeare's Henry IV
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A gossipy tale of an editor at home with royalty, behaving unlike a former president.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Clinton famously said he tried marijuana but 'didn't inhale', so anyone who did not copy him did.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinton's claim was not breathing in the smoke, so the person who breathed it in did the reverse.

clue.text: Trees, in comparison with wood's finish, are derived from the source

indicators.note: a word's finish is its final letter, which is the only part kept

blocks.note: firs are evergreen trees
than introduces a comparison
the last letter of wood

explanation.surface: A forestry observation that trees, compared with finished lumber, come straight from the source.
explanation.definitionFit: Firsthand information comes directly from its origin, not through intermediaries.

clue.text: Paraphrase concerning a drug

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
hash, short for hashish

explanation.surface: An instruction to restate something about a narcotic in other words.
explanation.definitionFit: To rehash is to restate old material in a new form, much as one paraphrases.

clue.text: Returning through mossy barbecue pit

indicators.note: through says the answer runs across the words that follow it
returning means coming back the other way, so read the letters backwards

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Coming back through a moss-covered barbecue pit in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barbecue pit' looks like one thing; 'pit' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a seemingly bottomless chasm, a very deep pit.

clue.text: Check location of interstate arrest, apprehending our rivals

indicators.note: apprehending means seizing and holding, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: US interstate highways are named with I, as in I-95
to nail a suspect is to catch them
us and them: the other side

explanation.surface: Police stopping someone on the highway, and catching our competitors in the act.
explanation.walkthrough: The excuse 'the check is in the mail' tells where a payment supposedly is.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock excuse for a late payment, 'the check's in the mail', gives the cheque's whereabouts.

clue.text: We have reached agreement after rethinking last idea

indicators.note: rethinking an idea reshapes it, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: Negotiators settle once they have reconsidered a final proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It's a deal' is the stock phrase said when a bargain is struck.

clue.text: Religious teacher in Southwest: "Do I exist?"

indicators.note: in places the question inside the compass abbreviation

blocks.note: compass abbreviation
the existential question am I?

explanation.surface: A guru in Arizona or New Mexico pondering his own existence.
explanation.definitionFit: A swami is a Hindu spiritual master, a religious teacher by title.

clue.text: Warden's clash keeping Yale student up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means reading the letters from bottom to top
keeping means holding inside, so one word goes into the other

blocks.note: to jar is to clash, as colours or opinions do
Eli is the nickname for a Yale student, after Elihu Yale

explanation.surface: A college warden's conflict with a Yale undergraduate who is staying up late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warden' could be a college officer; here it is a prison one.
explanation.definitionFit: A prison warden and a jailer both keep inmates locked up, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: They refer to women with a male chromosome in a Pennsylvania town

blocks.note: hers is a pronoun used for women
the male pronoun
the Y chromosome

explanation.surface: A grammar or biology remark about pronouns and chromosomes, set in a small Pennsylvania town.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is written so 'They' seems to be people; here it means words, the pronouns that refer to women.
explanation.definitionFit: Hershey is a town in Pennsylvania, home of the chocolate company of that name.

clue.text: Professor's helper eating stewed toads with Mexican food

indicators.note: stewing jumbles ingredients together, so these letters get mixed up
one thing eating another takes it inside, so the helper goes around

blocks.note: TA, teaching assistant
the letters of toads, mixed up

explanation.surface: A grad student has an unappetizing meal of stewed toads along with some Mexican food.
explanation.walkthrough: A TA is the teaching assistant who helps a professor in an American university.
explanation.definitionFit: A tostada is a toasted or fried tortilla with toppings, a classic dish of Mexican cuisine.

clue.text: Fortune comes to the United States? That's a difficult position to maintain

definitions.text: That's a difficult position to maintain

blocks.note: one's lot is one's fortune or destiny
standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A wry political remark that American good fortune is hard to keep up.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'position' sounds political or economic, but it is a cross-legged yoga pose.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a seated yoga posture with each foot on the opposite thigh, notoriously hard to hold.

clue.text: In retrospect, established oceans as a quick way to start communication

definitions.text: a quick way to start communication

indicators.note: looking back in retrospect means the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: laid as in laid down, set up
the deep is a poetic name for the ocean

explanation.surface: A historical note on how laying cables across the seas sped up communication.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces are joined and then the whole string runs backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed dial lets a phone place a call with one button, a fast way to begin talking to someone.

clue.text: Fade out, like a post?

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, telling us to rearrange the word before it

blocks.note: the letters of fade, rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about how a post might fade out of view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fade out' reads as one phrasal verb; split it, and 'out' is the signal. The definition plays on the idiom 'deaf as a post'.
explanation.definitionFit: The simile 'deaf as a post' makes a post the standard image of something that cannot hear.

clue.text: Fire-resistant creature recalled Communist war zone, unfortunately

indicators.note: recalled taken as called back, so the string of words runs in the opposite direction

blocks.note: red is the colour of communism
Nam is the soldier's name for Vietnam
alas expresses that something is unfortunate

explanation.surface: A veteran painfully remembering a communist battlefield and some creature found there.
explanation.walkthrough: All three pieces are reversed together as one string, so the last word of the clue supplies the start of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend held that the salamander could live in fire unharmed, so it is the mythical fireproof animal.

clue.text: Bum crawled with, um, a metalworking tool

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means poor or faulty, so the letters are in a bad order

blocks.note: taken as written
er and um are both sounds of hesitation

explanation.surface: A tramp crawled along holding, um, some piece of workshop equipment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bum' reads as a noun for a vagrant; it is an adjective meaning defective.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc welder joins metal pieces using an electric arc, a standard tool of metalwork.

clue.text: Incited or disrupted instruction

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so the preceding letters are mixed

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone either stirred up or interrupted a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A direction is an order or guidance on what to do, as is an instruction.

clue.text: Heading for California's draw?

blocks.note: surface reading: a title or headline for whatever attraction pulls people to California
setter's reading: the compass direction in which someone travels when bound for California from the rest of the US

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading' looks like a noun, a caption; it is the verb of travel. The question mark admits the pun, and 'draw' hints at the westward pull of California.
explanation.definitionFit: California is on the Pacific coast, so travelling toward it from most of America means going in the direction of the sunset.

clue.text: Where lunatics might have been placed, shuffled about with some repetition
Soft and easy makes for a precarious situation

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for soft
a light task is an easy one

explanation.surface: A paradox: being soft and easygoing actually leads to danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A plight is a dangerous or difficult predicament, a perilous state of affairs.

clue.text: Spoiled child is second-rate pest

blocks.note: B grade is second-rate
a rat is a pest

explanation.surface: An exasperated verdict that an indulged child is a second-rate nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A brat is an ill-behaved, overindulged youngster, the usual word for a spoilt kid.

clue.text: Great, as disperser!

indicators.note: the exclamation mark is a playful hint that the preceding letters will be scattered

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: Applause for someone who scatters things well.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition doubles as the signal: 'disperser' tells us to scatter the letters, and it also defines what crowd-control gas does.
explanation.definitionFit: Police use tear gas to break up crowds, so it is literally a crowd disperser.

clue.text: Excerpt from poem: "Blemish is a symbol"

indicators.note: an excerpt is a piece taken from a longer text, so the answer sits inside the words

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A line quoted from a poem declaring that a flaw carries symbolic meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: An emblem is a sign or device that represents something, which is a symbol.

clue.text: What the Rev. Robertson might say: "I left after inaugural, being unable to wait"

indicators.note: after the inaugural keeps only what follows the opening letter, dropping that first one

blocks.clueFragment: What the Rev. Robertson might say
blocks.note: Pat Robertson, the TV evangelist, introducing himself: I'm Pat
taken as written
went means left, departed

explanation.surface: The televangelist Pat Robertson announcing he walked out after an inauguration because he could not wait.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat Robertson was an American TV preacher. Only the letters of 'went' after its first survive.
explanation.definitionFit: An impatient person cannot bear delays, so 'unable to wait' is a direct paraphrase.

clue.text: Paul and I cooked a rice dish

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters of Paul and I, rearranged

explanation.surface: Two friends made a rice dish together for dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilau, also spelled pilaf, is rice cooked in seasoned stock, often with meat or vegetables.

clue.text: Cap on Pennsylvania city

blocks.note: a tam, or tam-o'-shanter, is a Scottish cap
postal abbreviation

explanation.surface: Imposing a limit on a Pennsylvania city, or a hat set on one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pennsylvania city' wants to be the definition; Pennsylvania is wordplay, and the city is in Florida.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a large city on Florida's Gulf coast, a plain example of a city.

clue.text: Came stumbling around average Arab city

indicators.note: stumbling suggests tripping into disorder, so the letters fall into a new order
around means the jumbled word is wrapped about the next piece

blocks.note: the letters of came, mixed up
a C grade is average

explanation.surface: A traveler arrives clumsily in an ordinary Arabian town.
explanation.definitionFit: Mecca, in Saudi Arabia, is the holiest city of Islam, in the Arab world.

clue.text: President of France stops short in nearby country

indicators.note: stopping short means falling just before the end, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: François Hollande, French president at the time of the puzzle

explanation.surface: The French president halts abruptly while visiting a neighbouring country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stops' looks like the verb of the sentence about a visit; it signals cutting off a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Holland, the common name for the Netherlands, lies close to France in northwest Europe.

clue.text: Taking advantage of one adopted by civil rights leader

indicators.note: being adopted means being taken in, so one thing goes inside the other

blocks.note: Martin Luther King, often written MLK, plus King
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone exploiting a person who was taken in by a famous civil rights leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The leader's initials and surname run together to make the outer string.
explanation.definitionFit: To milk a situation is an idiom for exploiting it fully for one's own gain.

clue.text: To begin with, you and me donning unmentionables for insufficient compensation

indicators.note: to begin with points at the opening letter of the word that follows
donning means putting on clothes, so these letters go inside the garment

blocks.note: unmentionables is a coy word for underwear
the first letter of you
taken as written

explanation.surface: A complaint that we were paid so little we were reduced to our underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: The short piece slips into the garment between its A and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Underpayments are sums paid that fall short of what is owed, so pay that is too low.
